# Ranks and General Protocol
Every Marine has a rank and a posting, though not every Marine has a position aboard the Halcyon. The Chain of Command normally places officers above enlisted in terms of following orders, but this may not be the case when NCOs (Non-Commissioned Officers) are assigned as FTLs. Regardless of position, though, an enlisted will always salute an officer, and an officer will always salute a higher-ranking officer. An enlisted will NEVER salute another enlisted but will come to attention in the presence of a Sergeant or higher in charge of a platoon. Respect and protocol go hand in hand.
Those who are for some reason unaware of their rank and position should consult a duty officer to rectify any missing paperwork.
## Command
The Colonel - This may either be a Colonel or a Lieutenant Colonel assigned to a post, and short of a General appearing on the scene, they are in charge.
The Captain - While this is unironically meant to be a Captain (and the XO of the Colonel), there may also on the very rare occasion be a Major holding this position. Rarely will there be a 1LT, in this situation they were most likely battlefield promoted.
The FTLs - This can be either an NCO or an Officer, as both have their own unique skill sets. NCOs start as low as Corporal and go as high as Master Sergeant. Some FTLs may be 2LTs as they gain experience to go on to become a Captain in charge of a unit.
Chain of Command (CoC) - A disciplinary tool to keep order in a unit. On Halcyon it follows from Colonel > Captain > FTL > Marine/Engineer/Corpsman>Borg, with Officer > Enlisted taking secondary priority.
## Enlisted Ranks
- E-0 Recruit (Rct) (You won't see any marines with this rank, only in boot camp.) - E-1 Private (Pvt.) - E-2 Private First Class (PFC.) - E-3 Lance Corporal (LCpl.) - E-4 Corporal (Cpl.) - E-5 Sergeant (Sgt.) - E-6 Staff Sergeant (SSgt.) - E-7 Gunnery Sergeant (GySgt.) - E-8 Master Sergeant (MSgt.) - E-9 Master Gunnery Sergeant (MGySgt) - E-9 Sergeant Major (SgtMaj) (Career enlisted, extremely rare) - E-9 Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps (SMMC) (Reserved for Winter Solstice / High Command)
## Officer Ranks
- O-1 2nd Lieutenant (2LT.) - O-2 1st Lieutenant (1LT.) - O-3 Captain (Cpt.) - O-4 Major (Maj.) - O-5 Lieutenant Colonel (LtCol.) - O-6 Colonel (Col.) - O-7 Brigadier General (BGen) - O-8 Major General (MGen) - O-9 Lieutenant General (LtGen) - O-10 General (Gen)
## Warrant Officers E-4 - E7 may become specialists in their chosen military occupational specialty. Warrant officers are also commissioned officers. Warrant Officers CWO3 - CWO5 are exceedlingly rare to see.
- W-1 Warrant Officer (WO) - W-2 Chief Warrant Officer 2 (CWO2)
## TSF Navy Corpsman Ranks - E-2 Hospitalman Apprentice (HA) - E-3 Hospitalman (HN) - E-4 Hospital Corpsman 3rd Class (HM3) - E-5 Hospital Corpsman 2nd Class (HM2) - E-6 Hospital Corpsman 1st Class (HM1) - E-7 Chief Hospital Corpsman (HMC)
